body.statement: Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:iid-sampling}\), \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\), \(\ref{ass:design-density}\), \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\), and \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), there is \(K<\infty\) such that, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), all \(d2^{d-1}\) risks and all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC values lie in their cross-fitted bands, with \(w_R\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n^2\}\) and \(w_H\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n\}\). Boundedness of the kernels controls the held-out empirical fluctuation in \(w_H\), while Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\) is used only to convert the cross-fitted residual error into the additive \(a_n\) term. On this event, if \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), every queried HSIC value belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and \(2w_H<\lambda\), then \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\). Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation never forces a binary label for an HSIC interval meeting both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\): it retains both labels and returns the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, which may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs.
body.justification: The finite-sample theorem ties singleton recovery to the primitive gain slack and an explicit pruning resolution while preserving abstention near the discontinuity at independence.
body.gap: Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) and Shekhar et al. (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) do not jointly cover learned normalized risks, simultaneous residual perturbations, adaptive insertions, and separated-model graph confidence sets.
body.consumer: Users receive a certified labelled DAG only when both navigation and pruning margins dominate propagated uncertainty.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and let \(\underline v\) be the constant in Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal X\) supplies a finite bound \(B\) for every coordinate of \(V\) and every clipped residual used below.  All constants denoted by \(K\), \(K_R\), or \(K_H\) may depend on \(B\), the fixed fold proportions, the Holder radius, the two design-density bounds, the kernel bounds, and \(L_k\), but not on \(n\), \(\alpha\), or the particular indices \((v,A,u)\).

We first construct the regression fits and record their simultaneous error.  Fix \(v\in I\), \(A\subseteq I\setminus\{v\}\), and put \(m=|A|\).  Partition \(\mathcal X_A\) into rectangles of side at most \(h\), use polynomials of total degree at most two on each nonempty rectangle, and clip their values to the coordinate range of \(V_v\).  Taylor's formula and Assumption \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\) give a member \(g_h\) of this sieve such that
\[
 \lVert g_h-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_\infty\le K h^3. \tag{1}
\]
There are at most \(K h^{-m}\) polynomial coefficients.  For completeness, the usual least-squares bound needed here follows by applying the exponential Markov inequality to the bounded loss differences on each cell and then summing over the cells: the conditional variance of a squared-loss difference is at most \(K\) times its excess squared-error risk, while the sum of the cell dimensions is at most \(K h^{-m}\).  Peeling according to dyadic values of that excess risk and summing the resulting geometric series gives, for the clipped empirical least-squares fit on a training fold of size proportional to \(n\),
\[
 \Pr\left[
 \lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2
 >K\left\{h^6+\frac{h^{-m}+\log(1/\delta)}{n}\right\}
 \right]\le\delta . \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, (1) supplies the comparison element in the empirical least-squares basic inequality; boundedness supplies the displayed variance--mean relation; and on a shell of population excess risk \(r\), the exponential bound is \(\exp\{-c n r+K h^{-m}\}\), which is summable once \(r\ge K\{h^{-m}+\log(1/\delta)\}/n\).  Thus (2) does not require an unrecorded tail or moment hypothesis.

Take \(h=t_n^{1/(m+6)}\) when \(t_n\le1\), and use \(\delta\) proportional to \(\alpha/M_d\).  Since \(m\le d-1\),
\[
 t_n^{3/(m+6)}\le t_n^{3/(d+5)}=a_n.
\]
A union bound over the \(d2^{d-1}\) regressions therefore yields, with probability at least \(1-c\alpha\),
\[
 \max_{v,A}\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}
 \le K a_n. \tag{3}
\]
When \(t_n>1\), clipping and enlargement of \(K\) give (3) directly because both the response and fitted regression are bounded.  Repeating the construction over the fixed number of cross-fitting folds changes only \(K\).

On an evaluation fold independent of a fitted regression, let \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) be the empirical mean of the squared fitted residual.  The defining orthogonality of conditional expectation in Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) gives, conditionally on the training fold,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!left[(V_v-\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A))^2\mid\widehat\mu_{v,A}\right]
 =R_{v,A}+\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2. \tag{4}
\]
The evaluation losses are conditionally independent and bounded.  For any centered random variable \(W\) with \(|W|\le b\), convexity of the exponential on \([-b,b]\) gives \(\mathbb E e^{sW}\le e^{s^2b^2/2}\); exponential Markov optimization and a union bound therefore give a simultaneous evaluation error at most \(K\sqrt{t_n}\).  Combining this fact with (3)--(4) produces intervals centered at \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) which contain every \(R_{v,A}\) and whose common half-width obeys
\[
 w_R\le K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n^2\}
 =K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}. \tag{5}
\]

For the HSIC coordinates, use the bounded, centered order-four V-statistic on the evaluation fold, with the off-fold residuals.  Conditional on the training fold, changing one evaluation observation changes this statistic by at most \(K/n\).  The same exponential argument, now exposed one observation at a time, gives deviation \(K\sqrt{t_n}\); terms with repeated indices contribute at most \(K/n\), which is absorbed into that bound.  It remains to compare the population HSIC of fitted and true residuals.  The population HSIC expansion is a fixed sum of expectations of products of bounded kernel factors.  Telescope each product at its residual-kernel factor and apply Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and (3) then give
\[
 \left|H_{\widehat\mu}(v,A,u)-H(v,A,u)\right|
 \le K\mathbb E_P\left|\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A)-\mu_{v,A}(V_A)\right|
 \le K a_n. \tag{6}
\]
Consequently simultaneous intervals contain all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant HSIC coordinates and satisfy
\[
 w_H\le K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n\}
 =K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}. \tag{7}
\]
The pruning coordinates have the form \(H(v,A,u)\) with \(u\notin A\).  Their number is at most another \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\), so the same union bound covers every possibly adaptive pruning query.  This replaces \(M_d\) by at most \(2M_d\); because \(M_d/\alpha\ge2\), \(\log(2M_d/\alpha)\le2\log(M_d/\alpha)\), and the change is absorbed into \(K_H\).  Allocating the preceding failure probabilities so that their sum is at most \(\alpha\) proves the asserted simultaneous coverage probability and the two displayed band rates.

We next make explicit the score-radius consequence that is implicit in interval propagation.  Work on the simultaneous coverage event, suppose all queried HSIC values belong to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), and suppose \(2w_H<\lambda\).  If \(H=0\), its interval has upper endpoint at most \(2w_H<\lambda\); if \(H\ge\lambda\), its lower endpoint is at least \(H-2w_H>0\).  Hence Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) returns the correct singleton label for every queried dependence indicator.

Assume also that \(w_R<\underline v/2\).  Write \(y_v=R_{v,\varnothing}=\operatorname{Var}_P(V_v)\) and \(x_{v,A}=R_{v,A}\).  Conditional expectation is the \(L^2(P)\) projection onto the functions of \(V_A\), so
\[
 0\le x_{v,A}\le y_v,
 \qquad y_v\ge\underline v. \tag{8}
\]
Let \(\widehat y_v\) and \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) be the risk-band centers, and project \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) onto \([0,\widehat y_v]\), denoting the result by \(\widetilde x_{v,A}\).  Coverage and \(w_R<\underline v/2\) imply \(\widehat y_v>0\).  Since \(x_{v,A}\in[0,y_v]\), clipping cannot increase its coordinatewise error, and the possible displacement of the upper clipping endpoint is bounded by \(|\widehat y_v-y_v|\); hence
\[
 |\widetilde x_{v,A}-x_{v,A}|\le w_R,
 \qquad |\widehat y_v-y_v|\le w_R. \tag{9}
\]
Define the feasible propagated center \(\widetilde q(v,A)=1-\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\).  By (8)--(9), \(0\le\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\le1\), and therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde q(v,A)-q(v,A)|
 &=\left|\frac{x_{v,A}}{y_v}-\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\right|\\
 &\le \frac{|x_{v,A}-\widetilde x_{v,A}|}{y_v}
 +\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\frac{|\widehat y_v-y_v|}{y_v}
 \le \frac{2w_R}{\underline v}. \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
For fixed singleton dependence labels, the multiplier \(1-D(v,A)/(|A|+1)\) in Definition \(\ref{def:gene-score}\) lies in \([0,1]\).  An insertion changes predecessor sets only for the moved node and nodes in the traversed block, at most \(d\) nodes.  Its gain is a difference of the before and after local contributions for precisely those nodes.  Summing (10) over at most \(d\) contributions on each side proves the deterministic propagation bound
\[
 w_S\le K_d w_R,
 \qquad K_d=\frac{4d}{\underline v}=O\!\left(\frac d{\underline v}\right). \tag{11}
\]
The factor four accounts for two local-score sums and the two risk coordinates in each normalized risk.  Thus no continuity of the independence indicator has been used: (11) is asserted only after the separated-label event has made every such indicator fixed.

Combining (5), (7), and (11), choose constants
\[
 K_1\ge \frac{8K_R}{\underline v},
 \qquad K_2\ge2K_H, \tag{12}
\]
enlarging \(K_1\), if necessary, to absorb the fixed regularity constants.  The two direct inequalities
\[
 K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},
 \qquad
 K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda \tag{13}
\]
imply, respectively, \(w_R<\underline v/2\) and \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and \(2w_H<\lambda\), after the constants are fixed.  The first implication uses \(d\ge2\) and, for the stated sample-size consequence below, \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\le1\).

At any non-topological order, Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) supplies a correcting insertion with true gain at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\).  Coverage and \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) make that insertion positive for every score table compatible with the bands.  Strict score ascent cannot revisit an element of the finite set \(\mathfrak S_I\), so every compatible terminal order is topological.  The now-singleton pruning labels coincide with the population labels used in Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\); that theorem therefore gives the labelled graph \(G_0\) for every compatible terminal path.  Taking their union proves \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\).

Finally suppose the regularity constants are fixed and \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},\lambda\le1\).  Put
\[
 \gamma_d=\max\left\{2,\frac{d+5}{6}\right\},
 \qquad \beta_d=\frac{d+5}{3}.
\]
Since \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d\le1\), making \(t_n\) a sufficiently small constant multiple of \((\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d)^{\gamma_d}\) controls both terms in the first inequality of (13).  Since \(\beta_d>2\) for \(d\ge2\), making \(t_n\) a sufficiently small constant multiple of \(\lambda^{\beta_d}\) controls both terms in the second.  Hence a direct sufficient sample size is
\[
 n\ge K\log(M_d/\alpha)
 \max\left\{
 \left(\frac d{\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}}\right)^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},
 \lambda^{-(d+5)/3}
 \right\}. \tag{14}
\]
The score-margin exponent equals two through \(d=7\), the two powers coincide at \(d=7\), and the nonparametric power \((d+5)/6\) governs for \(d>7\); this is the score-margin elbow at \(d=7\).  Equation (14) is a sufficient consequence of the proved bands and is not asserted to be minimax optimal.

Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation never forces a binary label for an HSIC interval meeting both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\): it retains both labels and returns the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, which may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs.  This is exactly the set-valued conclusion in Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\), and it completes the proof.
